title: Your First Blueprint
_code_source: The editor pane must show the blueprint exactly as block 2 of the wiki page has it (Status struct, gum_resource_manager, buy_gumball, get_status). Do not substitute a simplified sample - beats 06, 07 and 08 describe that specific code.
_voice_note: radix-studio/VOICE.md, read 2026-08-18 after its consolidation into one file. Essay preset for the arc (one governing analogy, open wide, close bigger); tweet-preset plainness at sentence level, because a listener gets one pass and cannot re-read. Governing analogy: custody against bookkeeping - a machine that holds its stock, not a ledger that remembers it.

beats.line: A vending machine either holds gumballs or it holds a promise about gumballs. Most smart contract platforms build the second kind. Scrypto builds the first.
Start with a package. That is the unit Scrypto deploys: one folder, with one or more blueprints inside it.
Six things land on disk. Open rust-toolchain.toml first, because it pins the Rust channel this package compiles with, and the pin depends on which radix-clis version generated the file.
The manifest names one dependency that matters. Scrypto itself, version 1.3.1.
Now the blueprint. Read it as a class the Radix Engine can load: a struct saying what the component owns, and an impl saying what it does.
Two vaults. A vault is permanent storage the engine controls, and it holds real resources rather than a number standing in for them.
ResourceBuilder mints a hundred gumballs once, at instantiation. They drop straight into a vault, and the component owns them from that moment.
Now look for the balance mapping. You will not find one. buy_gumball moves whole resources between containers, and the engine rejects any transaction that leaves a resource unaccounted for.
Scrypto compiles to WebAssembly, so every validator runs the same bytes and reaches the same answer. On macOS this step needs a wasm-capable clang, and Apple's ships without one.
Under a minute, and the package is built.
You have a component that holds its own inventory. Publish it to Stokenet next: the same package, on a public network. A machine that holds its stock, not a ledger that remembers it.
